current.text: Jaylen Brown is gone from Boston. Tatum is the top option and Paul George is the clear number two.
Experts expect a big usage season, with more usage than last season.
He came back from a torn Achilles much earlier than expected last season. He said he played at about 80 to 85%, yet he finished 19th per game and played 35 minutes a night in the playoffs.
His rim finishing fell from 69% to 60% after the Achilles return.
His FG% should go up, and the expert is fairly confident he returns to his best.

He missed playoff Game 7 with knee inflammation, which was called knee soreness. It came from compensating for the Achilles. It is not chronic and needed no surgery. He is expected to arrive fully healthy.
Most experts are not worried about the Achilles. The Game 7 knee problem is the only concern they raise, and one expert puts that risk at about 1%. Dan is more neutral on him because of the Achilles.
He is not expected to sit back-to-backs. That includes the three Boston has in the fantasy playoff window.
Boston has 16 back-to-backs, tied with Brooklyn for the most in the league. Three of them fall in the fantasy playoff window.
Boston's playoff schedule is 4-3-4 games in weeks 19 to 21, one game short of the maximum.
Experts rate him a first-round pick and are comfortable taking him at picks 6 to 8. Two recent mocks took him at pick 6. Dan sees him as one of many first-round players bunched together.
He went for 46 USD in an expert auction mock draft.
Josh would pay more than 45 USD for him in an auction.
Boston is projected to win about 48 games. Experts see it as a better regular-season team than last year.
Boston plans four shooters around a big in the dunker spot. Tatum will play only some small-ball center.

durable.text: He tore his Achilles in the 2025-26 season.
He was seen as an iron man before the Achilles tear.
Points are a league outlier. He also gives a forward high threes, rebounds and assists.
His turnovers are high for a forward.
Lloyd names blocks, steals and FG% as his weak categories.

note: Both sites rank him 7th and value him at 54 to 58 USD (Yahoo average cost 57.8 USD, ESPN 56.0 USD). An expert auction mock sold him for 46 USD, so a price in the high 40s to mid 50s is a fair buy in our league. His category profile is about 26 points, 3.3 threes, 8.9 rebounds and 5.6 assists from the F slot, with about 2.7 turnovers and a 45.5% FG%, so he fits punt TO builds best. Early in the season, check that his FG% recovers toward his old level and that he plays Boston's back-to-backs. The team has 16 of them, three in our playoff weeks.
